web_events.query: China PMI economic data this week
web_events.answer: China's producer prices surged to a 45-month high in April, rising 2.8% from a year earlier, driven by global energy price shocks from the Middle East conflict. This marks the second consecutive month of increase, ending a nearly four-year deflationary cycle. Meanwhile, China's export growth accelerated in April, rising 14.1% from a year earlier, up from a 2.5% increase in March. Consumer prices also ticked up 1.2% in April from a year earlier, surpassing economists' estimates of 0.9% growth.
